extracted.intended_audience: public water system owners/operators and State drinking water authorities responsible for compliance with the EPA Lead and Copper Rule
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for sampling, monitoring, public education, outreach, service-line replacement outreach, filter provision, waiver eligibility, and State reporting for lead and copper in drinking water under EPA Part 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory outreach when replacement rate not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If a water system does not meet their cumulative average replacement rate, the system must conduct outreach in the year following the program year for which the system does not meet the rate and annually thereafter until the system meets the cumulative average replacement rate or until there are no lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines remaining, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For community systems serving >3,300 persons the outreach must be one activity from paragraphs (h)(2)(i)-(iv) or two activities from (h)(2)(v)-(viii). For community systems serving ≤3,300 persons the outreach must be one activity from (h)(2)(i)-(viii). Allowed activities include: (i) conducting a public meeting; (ii) participating in a community event to provide information; (iii) contacting customers by phone/voice/text/email/door hanger; (iv) another State-approved method; (v) sending certified mail to affected customers/persons served at the service connection; (vi) social media campaign; (vii) media outreach (newspaper/TV/radio); (viii) visiting targeted customers (e.g., low participation areas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education and Distribution System and Site Assessment reporting to health agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: All community water systems must provide local and State health agencies with Distribution System and Site Assessment results and public education materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information to provide includes location of tap sample site that exceeded 0.010 mg/L, results of initial and follow-up tap samples, water quality parameter monitoring results, and any distribution system management actions or corrosion control adjustments (per §141.82(j)). Systems must annually send these materials for actions conducted in the previous calendar year no later than July 1 and may deliver by mail, email, or another State-approved method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for additional requirements — multiple lead action level exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that exceeds the lead action level at least three times in a rolling five-year period (based on tap samples per §141.86) must conduct the additional activities specified in this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first rolling five-year period begins on the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3). If the system exceeds the lead action level three times within any five-year period, the actions are required upon the third exceedance even if the five-year period has not fully elapsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of pitcher/point-of-use filters after multiple exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 60 days after the tap sampling period in which a water system meets the three-exceedance criterion, the system must make available to all consumers pitcher filters or point-of-use devices certified by an ANSI-accredited certifier to reduce lead, six months of replacement cartridges, and instructions for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The water system must continue to make replacement cartridges available until the system may discontinue the paragraph (j) requirements in accordance with paragraph (j)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter plan submission and contents after second exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 60 days after a water system exceeds the lead action level for the second time in a rolling five-year period, the water system must submit a filter plan to the State; the State must review and approve within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the system later meets the three-exceedance criterion, it is not required to re-submit the plan unless updates are made or requested by the State. The plan must include: (i) description of methods to make filters and replacement cartridges available (e.g., operating distribution facilities, delivering filters on request); and (ii) description of how the system will address barriers to consumers obtaining filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community outreach requirement after multiple exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system meeting the three-exceedance criterion must conduct a community outreach activity to discuss the multiple exceedances, steps the system is taking, consumer measures consistent with public education content, and how to obtain certified filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This outreach is in addition to the public education required under other sections. The system must conduct at least one activity from (j)(4)(i)-(v) within six months of the start of the tap sampling period after the most recent exceedance and at least one of those activities every six months thereafter until the system no longer meets the three-exceedance criterion. Allowed activities: public meeting; participate in community event; contact customers via phone/text/email/door hanger; social media campaign; another State-approved method. If already conducting an activity to meet paragraph (h), it may count for both unless State directs otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to discontinue multiple-exceedance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system may discontinue paragraph (j) requirements when it no longer has at least three lead action level exceedances in a rolling five-year period based on tap samples collected per §141.86.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A calculated 90th percentile at or below the lead action level based on fewer than the minimum required samples under §141.86 cannot be used to meet this discontinuation. States may allow earlier discontinuation if the system has taken actions to reduce lead (e.g., re-optimized corrosion control, completed service line replacement) and the system is at or below the lead action level for two consecutive tap monitoring periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site sample plan and sampling site identification
rubrics_metrics.description: By the start of the first tap monitoring period requiring lead and copper sampling, each water system must identify potential tap sampling sites and submit a site sample plan to the State as required in §141.90(a)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may require modifications. The system must identify a pool of sites sufficient to collect the number of tap samples required in paragraphs (c)(1) and (d)(1). To select sites, systems must use information on service line and connector materials (lead, copper, galvanized) collected under §141.84, and must select locations from the highest tier available unless the site is unavailable per paragraph (a)(4). Sampling sites cannot include taps with installed POE treatment or POU devices designed to remove inorganic contaminants, except when such devices are in place at all service connections for primary drinking water taps to meet other standards (§141.93(c)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement when fewer than five usable sampling sites
rubrics_metrics.description: If a water system has fewer than five sites meeting the sample site criteria to reach the required number of sites, the system must collect at least one sample from each tap and additional samples from those taps on different days to meet the required number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, the State may allow a reduced number of samples fewer than specified in (c)(1)/(d)(1) provided 100% of all taps that can be used for human consumption are sampled. The State must approve such a reduction in writing based on system request or onsite verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to sample at sites with lead premise plumbing or lead service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: A system serving sites with premise plumbing made of lead and/or served by a lead service line must collect all monitoring samples from those sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the system cannot identify enough such sites to meet the minimum required number, it must collect from every available such site and collect remaining samples per tiering requirements under paragraph (a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling tier hierarchy and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling sites must be selected from the highest tier available. Tier 1 is highest, Tier 5 lowest; sites are 'available' unless customer refuses or system made at least two outreach attempts without response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier definitions: (i) Tier 1: single-family structures with premise plumbing made of lead and/or served by a lead service line; (ii) Tier 2: buildings (including multiple-family residences) with premise plumbing made of lead and/or served by a lead service line; (iii) Tier 3: sites served by a lead connector or served by a galvanized service line or containing galvanized premise plumbing identified as ever downstream of a lead service line (Tier 3 for community systems includes single-family only); (iv) Tier 4: sites with copper premise plumbing with lead solder installed before the State's applicable lead ban (Tier 4 for community systems includes single-family only); (v) Tier 5: sites representative of distribution system (plumbing materials commonly found). Systems must report refusals/non-responses per §141.90(a)(2)(viii). If insufficient higher-tier sites, systems may sample next highest tier. For community systems where Tier 2 ≥20% of residential structures, Tier 2 may be used even when Tier 1 is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection protocol (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, all tap samples for lead and copper must be one liter in volume and have stood motionless in the plumbing/service line for at least six hours prior to collection, using wide-mouth one-liter bottles as defined at §141.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residential samples from interior kitchen or bathroom sink cold-water taps; non-residential from an interior cold-water tap typically used for human consumption. Systems may collect samples or allow public to collect after providing instructions; instructions cannot direct removal/cleaning of aerator or flushing prior to minimum six-hour stagnation. Samples may be acidified up to 14 days after collection; after acidification the sample must stand in original container per approved EPA method. If public sampling is allowed, the system cannot challenge sample accuracy based on alleged collection errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-liter and fifth-liter paired sampling for Tier 1/2 lead service line sites
rubrics_metrics.description: For sites served by a lead service line (Tier 1 and Tier 2), an additional fifth-liter sample must be collected at the same time as the first-liter sample and analyzed for lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To collect a first-liter-and-fifth-liter-paired sample, systems must collect water in five consecutively numbered one-liter wide-mouth bottles after at least six hours stagnation without flushing. Collect starting with bottle 1 through bottle 5; the first-liter sample is bottle 1 and the fifth-liter sample is bottle 5. The first-liter must be analyzed for lead and copper where both are required; where only lead is required the first-liter may be analyzed for only lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-approved sampling deviations and follow-up/consumer-requested samples
rubrics_metrics.description: State-approved samples collected per paragraph (b)(3) may include stagnation periods less than six hours but must meet other collection criteria. Systems may use different volumes/procedures for follow-up samples under §141.82(j)(2) and consumer-requested samples under §141.85(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer-requested samples must be collected in accordance with §141.85(c). Systems must submit results of these samples to the State per §141.90(a)(2)(i) and (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority to previous sampling sites and reporting site changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must prioritize sampling the same sites sampled in the previous tap sampling period. If a previous site no longer qualifies or access cannot be gained, the system must sample another site in its site sample plan meeting the original tiering criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must report any site changes and explanations per §141.90(a)(2)(v). If site sample plan changes are needed, systems must submit updated site sample plan per §141.90(a)(1)(i) before the start of the next tap sampling period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution request for insufficient six-hour stagnation sites
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-transient non-community water system, or a community water system meeting §141.85(b)(8), that cannot collect enough first-liter or first+fifth samples meeting the six-hour stagnation requirement may apply in writing to the State to substitute samples that do not meet the six-hour requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such systems must collect as many qualifying samples as possible and for remaining samples identify times/locations likely to result in longest standing times. The State has discretion to waive prior approval requirement either via regulation or written notification to the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard monitoring schedule and minimum number of sites by system size
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard monitoring consists of six-month tap monitoring periods beginning January 1 and July 1. During a standard period, systems must collect at least one sample from the number of sites specified by system size (table to paragraph (c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table (standard number of sites): >100,000 persons = 100 sites; 10,001–100,000 = 60; 3,301–10,000 = 40; 501–3,300 = 20; 101–500 = 10; ≤100 = 5. Standard monitoring sites must be selected per tiering in paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria triggering standard monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain systems must conduct standard monitoring for at least two consecutive tap monitoring periods following the monitoring period in which the trigger is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers include: (i) all systems with lead or galvanized requiring replacement service lines in inventory as of Nov 1, 2027 unless system already meets specific criteria (compliance monitoring targeting lead/galv lines, collecting samples per collection requirements, and collecting first-liter or paired samples); (ii) any system whose most recent 90th percentile lead and/or copper results as of Nov 1, 2027 exceed the action level; (iii) systems that exceed a lead or copper action level; fail to operate at/above minimum or within OWQP range for >9 days in any tap monitoring period; become a large system without corrosion control treatment (or similar); install or re-optimize OCCT or adjust OCCT after a Distribution System and Site Assessment; systems for which State designates new OWQPs; systems that install source water treatment per §141.83(a)(3); systems that notify State of upcoming new source or long-term change unless State deems not significant; systems without lead/galv lines that later discover such lines unless replaced before next period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced monitoring (annual/triennial) site minimums and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced monitoring is annual or triennial (each includes one tap sampling period). During reduced monitoring, systems must collect at least the number of sites specified in table 2 to paragraph (d)(1) unless specified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table (reduced minimum number of sites): >100,000 = 50; 10,001–100,000 = 30; 3,301–10,000 = 20; 501–3,300 = 10; 101–500 = 5; ≤100 = 5. Eligibility requires meeting all section requirements, including collecting at least minimum samples for at least two consecutive tap monitoring periods; State may require more frequent monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to reduce to annual monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system that does not exceed the lead and copper action levels and (for systems with State-designated OWQPs) also maintains the designated OWQP range for two consecutive six-month tap monitoring periods may reduce to annual monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems reducing to annual monitoring must sample at least the standard number of sampling sites for lead (paragraph (c)(1)) and at least the reduced number of sites for copper (paragraph (d)(1)). Prior to annual monitoring, systems must receive a written State determination approving annual monitoring based on review of monitoring, treatment, and other information per §141.90. The first annual tap monitoring period must begin no later than six months following the last tap monitoring period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to reduce to triennial monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Small/medium systems may reduce to triennial monitoring after three consecutive years of meeting non-exceedance and OWQP maintenance criteria; any system may reduce to triennial monitoring if it demonstrates for two consecutive tap monitoring periods that its 90th percentile lead ≤0.005 mg/L and 90th percentile copper ≤0.65 mg/L (and OWQPs maintained where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems on triennial monitoring must sample at least the reduced number of sites per paragraph (d)(1). Prior to triennial monitoring they must receive written State approval per §141.90. Timing rules for first triennial sampling period are specified (must begin no later than three calendar years after the last calendar year sampled).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tap sampling period timing under reduced monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Tap sampling period for reduced monitoring must occur within June–September unless State approves a different period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-approved alternative must be a continuous period no longer than four consecutive months, entirely within one calendar year, and represent normal operations when highest lead levels are likely. Special rules apply for non-transient non-community systems that do not operate June–September. Systems with State-approved alternate periods must complete next tap sampling period within specified months (21 months if annual; 45 months if triennial). Systems with waivers must follow specific nine-year collection rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion of samples for 90th percentile calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems and the State must consider results of any sampling conducted in addition to the minimum required samples when calculating the 90th percentile if the samples meet the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer-requested samples (§141.85(c)) must be considered if they meet (a) and (b). If multiple samples from the same site in the same tap sampling period meet the requirements, only the highest value from each site may be considered (except for systems under paragraph (a)(2)). If systems sample higher tiers to meet minimums, they may not then include additional lower-tier samples. Samples collected as part of Distribution System and Site Assessment (§141.82(j)(2)) and follow-up samples after service line replacement (§141.84(h)) cannot be included in the 90th percentile calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of samples and replacement sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample invalidated does not count toward 90th percentile calculations or minimum monitoring requirements. The State may invalidate a sample if: (i) lab error caused erroneous results; (ii) sample taken from a site that did not meet site selection criteria (e.g., higher-tier sites still available); (iii) sample collected in manner not meeting collection protocol; (iv) container damaged in transit; (v) substantial reason to believe sample tampered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To invalidate a sample the State must document decision and rationale in writing; cannot invalidate solely because a follow-up sample differs. If invalidation leaves too few samples to meet minimum requirements, the system must collect replacement samples as soon as possible but no later than 20 days after State notification or by end of the tap sampling period, whichever is later. Replacement samples taken after the end of the applicable tap sampling period can only be used to meet that tap monitoring period's requirements, not a subsequent period. Replacement samples must be taken at same locations as invalidated samples except when invalidated due to site selection error or lack of access; then replacement must be at locations meeting site selection criteria other than those already used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring waivers for systems serving ≤3,300 persons (materials & monitoring criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system serving ≤3,300 persons may apply to the State to reduce monitoring frequency to once every nine years if it meets materials criteria (distribution system and all drinking water plumbing free of lead- and/or copper-containing materials) and monitoring criteria (completed at least one six-month round of standard monitoring and demonstrates 90th percentile levels meet thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead materials criteria: system must certify/disclose no plastic pipes with lead plasticizers or plastic service lines with lead plasticizers; free of lead service lines, galvanized requiring replacement, lead connectors, lead pipes, lead soldered joints, and leaded brass/bronze fittings/fixtures unless such fittings meet 42 U.S.C. 300g-6(e) specifications. Copper criteria: certify no copper service lines or premise plumbing. Monitoring criteria: to qualify for lead waiver 90th percentile lead ≤0.005 mg/L; for copper waiver 90th percentile copper ≤0.65 mg/L. The State must notify system in writing of waiver determination and may place conditions (e.g., limited monitoring, periodic outreach). Systems must continue monitoring until they receive written waiver approval. Sampling frequency for approved waivers: at least once every nine years (samples collected no later than every ninth calendar year). Systems with partial waivers provide the materials certification when submitting tap sampling results.
